title: The Role of Family and Friends in Shaping Your Habits
coreMove: Choose or shape a group where the desired behavior protects belonging.
sourcePressure: Habits become more attractive when they align with belonging, social norms, and the people around us.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Claiming people blindly copy groups, instead of showing belonging changing what feels desirable.

hook: starting with a definition of close
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a robotics team normalizing teardown notes after every failed test
exampleSpecs.audience: a new member who hides mistakes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain cheers the messiest failure note, and the new member adds her own before packing up
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a robot chassis upside down on a pit table

exampleSpecs.domain: a synagogue walking group making punctual arrival the mark of care
exampleSpecs.audience: an older member trying to rebuild exercise
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether close-group norms pull the habit into identity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the group waits at the side door for anyone who texted by 6:55, and punctuality becomes part of being included
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a side door propped open before sunrise

exampleSpecs.domain: a tattoo studio apprentice adopting glove-change rituals from senior artists
exampleSpecs.audience: an apprentice watching what respected people do
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether prestige makes the safety habit attractive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she copies the senior artist changing gloves before touching the lamp, not because of a rule but because that is what pros do
exampleSpecs.firstImage: black nitrile gloves beside a wrapped lamp arm

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood birding club making field-note precision the price of being taken seriously
exampleSpecs.audience: a casual birder wanting acceptance by experts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the many define what good participation looks like
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after hearing three members compare timestamped notes, he adds weather and location instead of just bird names
exampleSpecs.firstImage: binoculars resting on a damp trail map

exampleSpecs.domain: a software incident room where senior engineers narrate calm rollbacks
exampleSpecs.audience: a junior engineer tempted to panic-deploy fixes
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the powerful model makes restraint desirable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she sees the respected lead pause, write the rollback plan, and gets status by copying composure
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a status board glowing red in a dark incident room

exampleSpecs.domain: a dance crew where everyone stretches before music starts
exampleSpecs.audience: a newcomer who usually skips mobility
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether group entry ritual makes warmup feel like belonging
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts she will skip stretching, then notices nobody touches the speaker until every mat is down
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rolled dance mats lined against a studio mirror

skillTargets: analyze how belonging makes habits attractive
choose social environments that normalize the desired action

tryThisNowSpec: Find one group where the behavior you want is normal. Put one of their visible norms in your path today.
